For a real object, a concave lens forms an upright diminished virtual image and a plane mirror forms an upright same-size virtual image. A convex lens forms an upright magnified virtual image when the object is inside its focal length.

tb-3A03-2.question:

B (2) only

Only a convex lens can produce inverted images.

Images of a distance object are formed on the focal plane.

∴ (3) is correct.

tb-3A03-3.question:

For any point on the object, some light rays from that point can still pass through the lower part of the lens and converge to form the image. Therefore, the whole image can be seen.

Some light rays are blocked on the upper part of the lens. Therefore, the image is dimmer.

tb-3A03-12.question:
Figure f shows two light rays, P and Q, of different colours passing through a lens L. Which of the following statements must be correct?

(1) L is a convex lens.

(2) P does not change its speed when it enters L.

(3) If P and Q are parallel to the principal axis before passing through L, they will converge to the same point on the principal axis.

A (1) only

B (1) and (3) only

C (2) and (3) only

D (1), (2) and (3)

tb-3A03-13.question:
A convex lens is placed in front of an object and an image is formed. The object distance is larger than the focal length. If another convex lens of the same size but with a shorter focal length is used, which of the following statements describing the situation is/are correct?

(2) The image distance decreases.

(3) The image becomes dimmer.

B (2) only

C (1) and (2) only

D (1) and (3) only
tb-3A03-13.reasoning:
For a convex lens, a real image is formed if the object distance is larger than the focal length.

If a convex lens with a shorter focal length is used, the object distance is still longer than the focal length.

∴ (1) is correct.

If u is unchanged while f decreases, v decreases.

∴ (2) is correct.

The lenses are of the same size, the same amount of light passes through the lenses. However, the image is smaller, so it is brighter.

∴ (3) is incorrect.
